g.text: Client-Server Model — connection lifecycle and where statelessness matters
Every request pays for a connection before it pays for anything else — and every app server behind the load balancer must be interchangeable.
session — a reroute doesn't log you out
HTTP/1.1 keep-alive & HTTP/2 reuse ONE connection —
you pay this once per connection, not once per request.
HTTP/3 (QUIC) folds the TCP+TLS cost into one exchange.
Server A holds your session in its own process memory.
Load balancer reroutes your NEXT request to Server B
(A got slow, or restarted for a deploy) —
B has never heard of your session. You're logged out.
Fix: either sticky sessions (fragile, undoes the point
of load balancing) or a shared store, as at left.
